summary: Promote the browser-submit gate out of per-ticket throwaways into `make browser`
description:
Shipped as `a9b81de` (2026-08-06) and **never created on the board** — the key was used in a
commit without a ticket file ever existing. Reconstructed 2026-08-08 during a board validation.

Makes the one quality gate this repo cannot automate into a command anyone can run:
`make browser`, backed by `scripts/browser.sh`, with specs committed under `test/browser/`
rather than written from scratch per ticket and thrown away.

**This is the substance of TKT-196**, which was still sitting in Backlog when this landed under a
different key. See the disposition comment on TKT-196.

**Why it could not be part of `make check`:** it needs the host's real Chrome, so CI cannot run it.
That is a property of the gate, not a gap in it — `AGENTS.md` now says so explicitly.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Created retroactively on 2026-08-08. The work was already on `main`; this ticket exists so the board's history is not missing a key that its own commits reference.

<!-- sdlc:stage=building kind=summary -->
### Implementation — `a9b81de` (2026-08-06)

`+545 / −79` across 13 files.

- **`make browser`** → `scripts/browser.sh` (98 lines), with `scripts/stack-env.sh` (68 lines)
  factored out so the browser gate and `scripts/smoke.sh` share one stack-environment derivation
  instead of duplicating it — `smoke.sh` shrank by 56 lines in the process.
- **`test/browser/reset-password.mjs`** (234 lines) — the first committed spec, submitting a real
  write path rather than only rendering it.
- **`AGENTS.md`** rewritten: the standing claim *"There is no Playwright/e2e harness in-repo yet"*
  is gone, replaced by the working agreement that a web-UI ticket which adds or changes a write
  form runs `make browser` and adds a spec.
- **A new learning**, `a-failed-optional-dependency-is-skipped-silently.md` (58 lines), plus an
  update to the existing browser-submit learning and `docs/development.md`.

**It immediately earned its keep:** TKT-226 used it to catch a `no-referrer` policy that nulled the
`Origin` header and 403'd every password reset, and TKT-224 used it to catch an undeclared 429 being
rewritten to 500 by the response validator — a defect no handler test could see, because handler
tests never cross the contract middleware.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### Closeout — TKT-228

Accepted by the owner 2026-08-08 (Gate 4), for work that shipped as `a9b81de` on 2026-08-06.

**No stage-duration table.** This ticket had no file on the board at all until 2026-08-08 — the key
appeared in a commit that referenced a ticket which was never created. Every stage here was
reconstructed after the fact, so there are no honest per-stage durations to report. **Excluded from
cycle-time analysis.**

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Shipped | `a9b81de`, 2026-08-06 22:47 -0700 |
| diff | `+545 / −79` across 13 files |
| PR | none — committed directly to `main` |
| Gates | none recorded; 4 granted 2026-08-08 |

**What shipped:** `make browser` → `scripts/browser.sh`, with `scripts/stack-env.sh` factored out so
the browser gate and `scripts/smoke.sh` share one stack-environment derivation — `smoke.sh` shrank by
56 lines. First committed spec: `test/browser/reset-password.mjs`. The standing `AGENTS.md` claim
*"There is no Playwright/e2e harness in-repo yet"* is gone, replaced by the working agreement.

**Verification.** `make browser` needs the host's real Chrome and cannot run in CI — that is a
property of the gate, not a gap in it. Not re-run on 2026-08-08. Accepted on the artifacts present on
`main` and on the two independent uses below, which are stronger evidence than a re-run would be.

**learnings:**
1. **The gate earned its keep twice within 48 hours, on defects nothing else could see.** TKT-226
   used it to catch a `no-referrer` policy that nulled the `Origin` header and 403'd every password
   reset. TKT-224 used it to catch an undeclared 429 being rewritten to 500 by the response
   validator. Both are SSR-layer failures that the API smoke suite passes straight through.
2. **A failed optional dependency is skipped silently** — captured as its own learning
   (`a-failed-optional-dependency-is-skipped-silently.md`) during the run.
3. **Promoting a throwaway into a gate is a decision that deserves its own ticket.** The TKT-190
   script proved the idea at ~90 lines and was deliberately not committed, because a new dev
   dependency plus a gate change should not be slipped into an authentication ticket.

**retro:**
- **A commit referenced a ticket key that did not exist.** Nothing rejects that today. The ticket
  key in a commit subject is the only link between the board and the code, and it is unvalidated in
  both directions — this ticket is the proof. A cheap pre-commit or CI check (`does .sdlc/tickets/
  <KEY>.json exist on sdlc-state?`) would have caught it at authoring time.
- **It delivered TKT-196's substance under a different key**, leaving TKT-196 in Backlog looking
  outstanding. Filing a fresh key instead of picking up the existing shaped ticket is what produced
  the duplicate. TKT-196 now carries a disposition comment and is left for its filer to close.
- **Residue:** the harness exists, but there is still **no committed spec for the three TKT-190
  staff-session behaviours** (`Origin` on same-origin POST, `SameSite=Lax`, cookie `Path=/admin`
  scoping) that motivated TKT-196 in the first place. Those were verified once by an uncommitted
  script and have been unverified since. Natural fit for TKT-195.
